prompt: In many towns and cities, online retailers have taken a large share of the trade that once went to shops on the high street. Do the advantages of this shift outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
Nowadays, most of the people prefer to do their shopping on the internet instead of going to the shops in the town centre. Because of this, many high street shops are closing down. This essay will discuss the advantages and the disadvantages of this change.

There are many advantages of the online shopping. First of all, it is very convenient. The customers can order anything from their home at any time, and they do not need to travel to the town or to find the parking. Secondly, the prices are usually cheaper on the internet, because the online shops do not pay the expensive rent, and also it is very easy to compare the price of the different websites. Furthermore, the choice is much bigger. In a normal shop there is a limited space, but on the internet the customers can find everything they want.

However, this change has also created the problems. The main problem is that many shops in the high street are closing, and the people who work there lose their job. This is bad for the local economy. Another problem is that the town centres are becoming empty and unattractive, and some people say they are not safe anymore in the evening. Also, the old people who can not use the internet very well are having the difficulties, because their local shops are disappearing.

In conclusion, the online shopping has the big advantages like the price, the choice and the convenience, but it has also the disadvantages for the town centres and the workers. Both sides have the strong arguments.
title: Online shopping and the high street
